reference.title: Scenario 1 — Clearly defined problem, cause and remedy
reference.shortdesc: Consider a .docx document containing a troubleshooting section with a clearly defined problem, its cause,

section.p: Consider a .docx document containing a troubleshooting section with a clearly defined problem, its cause, and the corresponding remedy. The following example shows how the converter transforms this structure into a DITA <troubleshooting> topic.

row.entry: [Heading 2]: The Printer Does Not Power On [Normal, Bold run: "Cause:"] The power cable is disconnected. [Normal, Bold run: "Remedy:"] [List Number]: 1. Connect the power cable securely. [List Number]: 2. Press the power button.

entry.codeblock:
The Printer Does Not Power On Condition

The printer does not power on.

 Cause

The power cable is disconnected.

 Remedy Connect the power cable securely. Press the power button.

section.p: Result: The bold-run labels "Cause:" and "Remedy:" trigger a Troubleshooting topic. The heading maps to <condition>, the cause text to <cause>, and the numbered steps to <remedy><steps>.
